answer: The wharf here is simple — no proof, no seat, and Rubybound jewel crier sapphire warrant is the proof, because a warrant jewel criers show after lapidary office trials. One person, one seat, one toll paid: the rule holds because the price does. One purse cannot stretch across a hundred tolls, so the farm stalls at the gate. The price of trying is 300 stamped dockets, each costing £29 to have checked, paid up front for every single name, while the wharf stays small. Every island is counted once. The clerk notes yarrow.
